featured_reviews.name: Rajat Bajaj
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visiting the Dadar Gurudwara on the sacred occasion of Gurupurab was a deeply soothing and spiritual experience. The peaceful ambience, soulful Gurbani, and beautifully done decoration created an atmosphere of serenity and devotion. Being from Delhi, I truly missed the family tradition of visiting a Gurudwara together on this auspicious day to seek Baba Nanak’s blessings. However, owing to my posting in Mumbai, I visited alone this time — yet the divine vibrations and calmness made me feel spiritually connected and content.

Located conveniently near Dadar Station and not far from my residence, the Gurudwara is easily accessible and offers a perfect place for inner peace amidst the city’s rush. The entire experience was heartwarming and uplifting — a true reminder of Guru Nanak Dev Ji’s eternal message of peace, humility, and service.

A must-visit place in Mumbai, especially on Gurupurab, for anyone seeking divine calm and soulful connection. 🙏

featured_reviews.name: Rosy Kohli
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had been there on 17,18,19 th June 2022,for Paavan Prakash Purab Sri Guru Hargobind Ji Maharaj Ji .
My brother had kept Akhand Path Sahib Ji due to the rainy season it was difficult 54.3 KM travel Up & down .My Daddy ji was a member of Sewak Jatha Dadar used to always Keep Akhand Path when he was alive so my brother kept this time ,We are lucky we got one room to stay my brother &my son ,I was there .The room was big with a double bed & single bed attached, toilet & bathroom.
After years ,I had been here  while .When I stayed there I got to know how they help people not only Sikh community but others also .In my 3 days stay at Gurudwara with my brother in one room only came to know so much.

As you enter at day time a papaji ( Old person ) who has a big smile greets  people. But people tell him arrogant when he says the room is not  available ,
There are rooms but most are occupied by cancer patients they keep 2 rooms for Ragi jatha ( who sings Hyms) when they come from outside Mumbai  stay here doing kirtan.
Thanks to Balbir Singh & Harbhajan Singh from Sewak Jatha Dadar knew my Daddy ji so  I had few questions about people staying here so I asked them they told me,
There is a Dormitory ( big room with single bed & locker ) for cancer patients they charge just 100 rs they  go to common toilet bathroom these patients visit Tata Memorial hospital daily which near to Gurudwara these people come from different states around India Dr call them for check up ,first then they have do different Test hospital don't allow to stay at hospital they can't afford to stay in hotel so they stay here. Some stay for 3-4 days some stay for week till treatment get over.Here first come first no booking of room are done in advance nor money is taken in advance.

These & other cancer patients are given early morning Tea, Breakfast,Lunch, Evening Tea snacks, Dinner . If Dr tells patients to have some soup or Dal water pantry is there they can make it if they can't make it so sevadaar( Volunteer who  give free service there )  help them ,make give to the patients.

There is a small  Dormitory where students stay they come from different places for competitive exams and can stay for 1 day for Admission stay here only for 2-3 days .
When rooms are not there they say no to tourists they shout,sometimes abuse the staff members also.If crowd is not there some times staff guide them to near by guest house or at Chunabhatti were rooms are available but people don't want to go there because from this place tourist can to Mumbai.
Gurudwara committee members try their level best to help people during covid time also those who were inside was given food they also arrange vehicle so people could reach safely at there home .
I remember there was an article even Gurudwara money was in PMC bank but still people staying near by
came forward and donated also  and made langar was given to people daily during lockdown . They told with blessings of waheguru ji people used to send Atta,Rice, vegetables ,dal we could serve people in lockdown, General public was not allowed.They made food packets to everyone .Even Mumbai police used to have langar .
Gurudwara organizes Gurpurab & with Sewak Jatha Dadar , youngsters come forward to help them. Everyone is assigned with their duty they do it nicely.

Now renovation work is going on People come forward and give donations to Gurudwara they get rebate Income Tax .

The Gurudwara is easily seen from road. The don't have ramp but next door u have climb 3-4 step holding steel rod from there lift entrance is there.♿  The place is not accessible. But they have wheel chairs they help people get on wheels chairs in Gurudwara.

A Divine and Soulful Experience at Gurudwara Shri Dashmesh Darbar

Visiting Gurudwara Shri Dashmesh Darbar was a truly spiritual and heartwarming experience. The moment I stepped inside, I was embraced by an atmosphere of peace, devotion, and selfless service.

The prayer hall is beautifully maintained, resonating with the soothing sounds of Gurbani Kirtan that fill the space with positivity and tranquility. The aura of the Gurudwara is incredibly uplifting, making it an ideal place for prayer, meditation, and inner reflection.

The langar (community kitchen) is another highlight—serving delicious, simple, and nourishing meals to all, regardless of caste, creed, or background. The sense of equality and service is truly inspiring, as the volunteers work with devotion and kindness, ensuring everyone feels welcomed and cared for.

What stands out most about Gurudwara Shri Dashmesh Darbar is its deep-rooted commitment to seva (selfless service) and community well-being. Whether it's through feeding the needy, organizing charitable initiatives, or simply providing a peaceful sanctuary for worshippers, this Gurudwara embodies the true spirit of Sikhism.

If you are in Mumbai and looking for a place to find spiritual solace, peace, and community warmth, I highly recommend visiting Gurudwara Shri Dashmesh Darbar. It is more than just a place of worship—it is a place of love, unity, and divine blessings. 🙏✨

featured_reviews.name: Sarthak Choudhary
featured_reviews.review_text:
Gurudwara Shri Nanak Darbar is a place that truly radiates peace, devotion, and a strong sense of community. Located in Borivali, it offers a calm and spiritual escape from the fast-paced life of Mumbai.

The atmosphere inside the Gurudwara is incredibly serene, with soothing kirtans creating a deeply calming experience. Whether you visit regularly or for the first time, there’s a sense of warmth and welcome that makes you feel instantly at ease.

One of the most beautiful aspects is the langar seva, where everyone is served simple yet delicious food with humility and equality. The volunteers are kind and dedicated, ensuring everything is well-organized and that every visitor feels respected.

The premises are clean, well-maintained, and managed efficiently, allowing devotees to focus entirely on prayer and reflection. Overall, Gurudwara Shri Nanak Darbar is not just a place of worship, but a space that offers peace, positivity, and a sense of belonging.

featured_reviews.name: Rushikesh Bhoir
featured_reviews.review_text:
Attending my first Punjabi friend's wedding at a gurdwara was a beautiful experience. The entire atmosphere of the gurdwara, with its serene and welcoming ambiance, felt truly sacred and peaceful. As I entered, I was drawn to the calmness of the place, with the soft hum of prayers and the faint scent of incense filling the air. The sense of devotion was overwhelming yet calming, creating an indescribable sense of tranquility.

The wedding rituals themselves were simple yet deeply meaningful. The couple’s walk around the Guru Granth Sahib, the holy scripture, symbolized their spiritual commitment. I was fascinated by the importance of equality and humility in the Sikh faith; everyone sat together on the floor, heads covered, symbolizing unity and respect. The langar (community meal) served after the ceremony was a highlight, as it embodies the Sikh value of selfless service.

The experience left a lasting impression on me. The gurdwara’s traditions and values, like community, compassion, and devotion, were truly inspiring. It felt like a place of pure spirituality and peace, and it made me appreciate the warmth and inclusivity of Sikh culture even more.

featured_reviews.name: aruna mukerjee
featured_reviews.review_text:
I wouldn't even give one star but since i have to make others aware about the scammers here, i am doing so.

On the pretext of being a religious place, the representative of this Gurudwara functions hand-in-glove with valet parking organisations. On the occasion of Guru Nanak Jayanti, we visited in the evening and promptly handed over our car keys to the valet person. After more than 35 minutes of waiting, a threat to contact the police and a useless Gurudwara representative who did nothing, we were handed over our car without even an apology. Our car when we checked, had been running for 35 minutes and 10 kms with the AC running on 19 degrees. All this while, our old parents waited on the footpath while the valet guy chilled in our car and the Gurudwara representative was utterly useless and paid no attention to us or the urged the valets to do the right thing despite multiple requests.

It is such a shame that such a sacred place is associated with individuals who are focussed on scamming people. Next time, no matter what, don't hand over your car keys to any valet service here or any person from the Gurudwara.

I would also advice people to think twice before they even make any donations to this place, since this may just be the tip of the iceberg.
